name: 475. A body above the large-payload threshold is converted like a small one (large payload conversion)
description: Fork contract C4/C5 for bodies above the large-payload threshold, TXE-7082. Local fixture regression, no live provider calls: start tests/e2e/api/runners/provider-error-fixture.mjs, start an isolated gateway on tests/e2e/api/provider_config/provider-error-fixture.config.json and run with providerErrorFixture=1; every case is skipped otherwise. Bifrost has two optimizations that skip its converters for a large body: a large request is streamed to the vendor unparsed, and a large response is streamed to the caller unparsed. Both are switched on by a transport hook that this gateway does not install, and where they are on, core now allows them only for a request whose vendor takes the caller's wire format unchanged (schemas.DecideLargePayloadEligibility). These rows pin what a caller of the unified /v1 routes gets from the gateway as shipped. Cohere is the provider because both directions depend on conversion: the unified task_type has to become Cohere's input_type, and Cohere sends no usage object, so usage.prompt_tokens exists only when Bifrost converts meta.billed_units. Row 1 is the small request. Row 2 sends the same request with an 11 MB input, above the 10 MB default threshold: the vendor still receives input_type and the caller still receives usage. Row 3 gets an answer above 10 MB from the vendor: the caller still receives usage and the whole vector. The refusal of a staged large request (413 before any upstream write) and the raw paths that remain need the hook, so they are covered by Go tests: core/largepayload_eligibility_test.go, core/schemas/largepayload_test.go and transports/bifrost-http/integrations/anthropic_native_passthrough_test.go.
